references.source: Gruson–Serganova, A Journey Through Representation Theory, 2018
references.locator: Chapter 2, section 6: Lemmas 6.1 and 6.3, Example 6.2, Corollaries 6.4–6.5 and Theorem 6.7.
references.comparison: Example 6.2, printed page 37, identifies induction of the trivial representation with the coset permutation representation. It is not a lemma.

Lemma 17.6 allows an arbitrary normal subgroup; Corollary 17.7 specializes to an abelian normal subgroup. The isotypic-block transitivity, stabilizer and induced-module argument concludes on page 40. This supplies one direction, not the whole two-sided Clifford correspondence independently proved in the lesson.

Page 40 introduces Brauer induction and refers its proof elsewhere. Page 41 states integral generation by inductions of one-dimensional representations from elementary subgroups. These pages are a statement comparison, not the full proof provider; the lesson retains its own full argument.

references.source: Gruson–Serganova, A Journey Through Representation Theory, 2018
references.comparison: The lemmas are 1.13, 1.15, 1.18 and 1.19; 1.14 and 1.16 are corollaries; 1.17 is an exercise. The lesson already correctly cites Corollary 1.16 in its proof.
